trajectory_summary: This is an efficient, cooperative call that reaches a booked in-person appointment in under nine minutes, but the efficiency comes at the cost of depth: the rep moves through verify items quickly without flipping the two strongest openings the customer handed him — a recent foot surgery disclosure and unprompted ROI/incentive skepticism. The booking itself is clean on time and date but structurally fragile because the customer twice showed she didn't fully track what the appointment was or who'd be attending.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (09:30) are agreed and confirmed by the rep at 06:57 ('Tomorrow at 09:30'), and a text follow-up is promised — this is a clean booked outcome despite the surrounding expectation-gap texture.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: I don't know, 50 and $60 because we're not using heat.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures the bill figure and immediately pivots to a logistical note about the bill not being representative yet ('we'll just build it off square footage') rather than using the number, or her own projection of a higher winter bill, as leverage to build urgency for tomorrow's appointment.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: I've always been interested in solar, but, the thing right now is, for years, I didn't have my own place. Now I have my own place, and I'm allowed to I'm allowed to do that.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asks the interest question early and gets a genuine, specific reason (long-standing interest, newly enabled by home ownership), but never references this back later in the call — not at booking, not at button-up, and not in the promised follow-up text framing.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Closing the appointment-expectation gap before button-up
primary_coaching_focus.quote: All I needed was a quote. You have to come out and measure or something?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer books a specific day and time but her own words at 06:14 and again at 08:01 show she never fully understood what she was agreeing to — an in-person visit from a specialist, not Carter, not a remote quote. This is the single biggest risk to the appointment holding, and it recurs twice.

key_moments.quote: I've had foot surgery, so I've been home for about six weeks.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer volunteers a health disclosure unprompted while explaining her availability. The rep's next line jumps straight to scheduling logistics with no acknowledgment.

key_moments.quote: And with all the government changes going on, I ain't counting on them at all.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a live cost/incentive-skepticism objection. The rep's response references 'new programs' but never flips her skepticism into urgency or curiosity about her specific numbers.

key_moments.quote: is there anyone else on the title of the home with you?
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer's answer is genuinely tangled (a tax-related co-title situation) and the rep accepts 'I'm the owner' at 02:01 without confirming whether the other person on title needs to be part of the appointment.

key_moments.quote: All I needed was a quote. You have to come out and measure or something?
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer's question reveals she booked expecting something different (a remote quote) than what's actually scheduled (an in-person visit). This is a real, unresolved expectation gap at the moment of booking, not just a procedural skip.
